title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 143 (Powers and duties of auditors and auditing standards)

content.overview: Every auditor of a company shall have a right of access at all times to the books of account and vouchers of the company, whether kept at the registered office of the company or at any other place and shall be entitled to require from the officers of the company such information and explanation as he may consider necessary for the performance of his duties as auditor. The auditor shall make a report to the members on the accounts examined and on every financial statement laid before the company, stating whether the statements give a true and fair view and dealing with the other matters the section lists. Fraud involving an amount at or above the prescribed limit is reported to the Central Government.
content.glance: Auditor has access to books and explanations, reports true and fair view to members, and reports fraud at or above the prescribed amount to the Central Government.
content.study:
## Section 143 — Powers and duties of auditors

**Access.** Right of access at all times to books of account and vouchers; right to require information and explanations from officers.

**Report to members.** Report on accounts examined and every financial statement laid before the company — whether true and fair view, and other matters listed in the section and rules (including internal financial controls where applicable).

**Fraud reporting (subsection (12)).** If the auditor has reason to believe that an offence of fraud involving an amount at or above the prescribed amount is being or has been committed against the company by officers or employees, report to the Central Government within the prescribed time. Below the threshold, report to the Board or audit committee as provided.

**Auditing standards.** Comply with the auditing standards as applicable.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Must every suspected irregularity be reported to the Central Government under section 143(12)?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only fraud involving an amount at or above the prescribed threshold is reported to the Central Government. Below that, the Board or audit committee route applies as provided.

misconceptions.trap: Treating every irregularity as a Central Government fraud report.
misconceptions.correction: Only fraud at or above the prescribed amount is reported to the Central Government under subsection (12).
